facts.name: Virginia Bluebells
facts.light: Part shade to shade; moist soil
facts.notes: Goes fully dormant by early July, so tuck it between ferns or phlox that will fill the gap. Often sold as dormant roots.
facts.buyNote: Virginia bluebells are often sold as dormant roots.

sources.title: Wild Ginger Woodlands (Michigan nursery): Virginia Bluebells
sources.note: Threatened in Michigan; seed from Michigan.

sources.title: Penn State Extension: Spring Ephemerals for Residential Gardens
sources.note: Virginia bluebell foliage dies back by summer, so interplant with hostas or ferns; mayapple goes dormant in summer, so pair it with ferns or late-summer flowers.

companions.why: Combines with bleeding heart and celandine poppy; hosta, astilbe, bugbane, Solomon's seal or ferns fill the gap after it goes dormant.
